title: Forge transport retry policy direction
rationale: pr-merge's direction (retry network/5xx/429, other 4xx fatal) beats pr-open's inverse because a 401/403 must surface an expired credential loudly per forge-contract §4, not be retried into silence

name: forge-p1-migration-recipe
description: Phase-1 migration recipe (steps 2-5 of pl-d1c9): replace private GITHUB_API_BASE/buildHeaders/readJson/readText/truncate copies with src/forge/github/ requestGitHub + GITHUB_API_BASE + readJson; map GitHubHttpError kind network->network else http_error to preserve the caller's existing result taxonomy; pass userAgent + a short context label. Adopting the shared retry policy adds retry where none existed — tests must supply maxRetries+1 canned failure responses (recordingFetch throws when exhausted). The domain PR-body clamp is clampPrBodyLength in pr-template.ts; annotate paths re-clamp through it, never inline.

title: Per-call-site retry adoption on the forge transport
rationale: One shared policy direction (transient=network/5xx/429, 4xx fatal), but whether in-band retries run depends on whether an outer poller already owns retry for that call.

content: warren-2740: scripts/acceptance/lib/github.ts imports buildGitHubHeaders/GITHUB_API_BASE from src/forge/github/. check:layers does not walk scripts/, so importing the seam (not re-implementing) keeps api.github.com literals out of scripts/ without widening WALK_ROOTS. GITHUB_TOKEN ownership: bootInProc PASSTHROUGH_ENV_KEYS passes it to the booted warren, which owns it (auto-open-PR, CI-fixer poller, push auth); the harness borrows it only for scenario 35 cleanup. Scenario 12 blanks it via extraEnv; 26/36 use WARREN_GH_FETCH_OVERRIDE=merged.

name: forge-transport-migration-recipe
description: Forge phase-1 transport migrations (plan pl-d1c9): consumers call requestGitHub from src/forge/github/http.ts with userAgent + context label, import GITHUB_API_BASE from headers.ts, and expose a retry?: GitHubRetryOptions passthrough so tests inject sleep:async()=>{} to stay fast. Shared recordingFetch/jsonResponse helpers live in src/forge/github/test-helpers.ts; jsonResponse takes (status, body), opposite of several legacy local copies.

Dispatching a plan's children as sequential warren runs collides in .seeds/issues.jsonl on every PR after the first: .gitattributes sets merge=union, which for a JSONL whose rows are rewritten in place (closing one issue rewrites blockedBy on every plan sibling) silently emits two contradictory copies of every touched row and reports a clean merge. 8 dup rows on the first collision, 20 on each later one across pl-d1c9's 19 children.
resolution: Resolve by taking the closed status where either side closed and INTERSECTING blockedBy across the two rows — each side only ever removes a blocker, so taking either row alone resurrects one the other side already satisfied (seen on umbrella seed warren-3fe7, where main dropped warren-4e78 and the branch dropped warren-0993). Verify with 'jq -r .id .seeds/issues.jsonl | sort | uniq -d' after every merge, then 'bun run check:seeds-integrity'. Filed warren-9c90 (merge driver) and warren-db8c (denormalized blockedBy).

name: plan-child-dispatch-prompt
description: Dispatch prompts for a plan child whose seed description is only a plan backref stub must name the design-doc SECTION as the spec, not the seed. pl-d1c9's 19 children all carry identical stub descriptions; the real spec is docs/design/forge-contract.md. Prompts citing exact sections (§6.1 drift inventory, §6.5 retry disagreement, §6.14 token gap) produced agents that made and DOCUMENTED the intended judgment calls; the seed alone specifies nothing.

title: Forge transport retry adopts the pr-merge direction
rationale: forge-contract §3 assigns semantic retry to the domain and transport retry to the forge. Retrying 4xx inside transport hides the expired-credential 401/403 signal the §4 credential campaign must surface loudly, so transport treats non-rate-limit 4xx as fatal.

description: Pushed a known-corrupt .seeds/issues.jsonl to main during the pl-d1c9 wrap-up. check:seeds-integrity had just failed with exit 1, but the gate and 'git push origin main' were chained with ';' not '&&', so the push ran anyway and succeeded. Its output line 'remote: - 2 of 2 required status checks are expected.' appears on a SUCCESSFUL push to a protected branch and was misread as a rejection, so the subsequent local dedupe+amend never reached the remote.
resolution: Repaired with a follow-up commit (b4612106) that re-applied the dedupe on top of origin/main; verified all six phase-1 closes and four new issues intact. Rules: chain a gate to the action with '&&' never ';'; treat 'required status checks are expected' as informational, not a rejection; and confirm any .seeds push by re-reading the file from origin (git show origin/main:.seeds/issues.jsonl | jq -r .id | sort | uniq -d) rather than trusting push output. Filed warren-53c0 for a pre-push hook, since a direct push to main bypasses CI where this gate normally runs.

description: Steered a running pi agent via POST /runs/:id/steer to add scope mid-run. The API returned 200, a steer.sent event landed on the run at seq 1615 with the full body intact, and the agent never saw it: zero mentions of the steered content across 187 state_change / 46 tool_use / 21 thinking / 14 text events in the 25 minutes after delivery, and the resulting PR contained none of the steered scope. steer.sent only asserts warren SENT the message; there is no delivery or ack event, so every signal available to the operator reads as success.
resolution: Do not assume a steer landed. Verify from the run's event stream that the agent actually referenced the content (jq over /runs/:id/events, which is NDJSON not an array), and if the run is nearly done, plan to apply the change by hand on the PR branch instead. Note the two-inbox split: POST /runs/:id/steer goes to runtimeProvider.sendMessage (the per-burrow inbox, hence runId:null in the response), while GET /runs/:id/inbox reads repos.runInbox, a DIFFERENT store — so an empty inbox GET is not evidence of delivery, and that route MUTATES on read so checking it can drain the real queue. Filed warren-3305.

name: forge-reap-pr-pipeline
description: Reap-pipeline Forge migration shape (warren-45e6)

content: src/runs/reap/test-helpers.ts fakeForge() is a FakeForge whose parseRepoRef also claims the github.com test URL (instance-method override); stubForge(overrides) is a contract-typed stub delegating to FakeForge with per-method overrides for failure kinds (conflict retry queues, no_credential) and capability flips. Never hand-rolled fetch mocks in reap tests. Both cancel inline-reap sites (plan-runs.ts, pause-resume.ts) route through cancelRunWiring — binding deps.forge there migrates both.

name: forge-merge-gate-consumption
description: warren-63e7 (plan-run merge gate onto Forge): the domain polls a stored PR webUrl via forge.parseRepoRef + a forge-neutral trailing-numeric-segment read for PullRequestRef.number — never joins owner/repo/number to a host path (forge-contract.md section 0). Providers' parseRepoRef must round-trip their own PR web URLs (FakeForge strips /pulls/<n>; GitHubForge handles /pull/<n>). Loud-notice policy: unauthorized/forbidden -> once-per-repo logger.warn keyed in a boot-scoped Set inside the checker closure; no_credential stays quiet stall-and-log; only not_found is fatal (isFatalForgeError).

name: forge-p3-domain-migration
description: forge p3 migration recipe (warren-0b49): domain pollers take the boot-resolved Forge (never a captured token/fetch seam); capability flags gate BEFORE any forge call (poller stays idle) with the ProjectHealTracker notice-gate as the once-per-project rate limit; git credentials are minted per-spawn via mintGitCredentialSecret at the server layer and passed down as plain secrets; tests use FakeForge with fake:// PR urls and Object.defineProperty to flip readonly capability flags.

name: fake-forge-state-file-seam
description: warren-2600: cross-process FakeForge seam — WARREN_FAKE_FORGE_STATE_FILE backs FakeForgeStore (reload-before-read, atomic tmp+rename persist-after-write) so acceptance scenarios driving a subprocessed warren can observe/merge PRs; scripts/acceptance/lib/fake-forge.ts startFakeForgeAutoMerge plays GitHub's auto-merge role. Falsification finding: POST /projects' github-only parseGitHubUrl was the ONE registration-boundary leak a forge swap hit — fixed via parseForgeOwnedUrl fallback (layout-only segments, src/projects/url.ts), outside forge-contract.md §0's named domains.

name: per-spawn-git-credential-mint
description: Per-spawn git credentials (forge-contract.md §4.2): mint via mintGitCredentialSecret(forge, project.gitUrl) immediately before the spawn, render with githubCredentialGitEnv, never store on a config object. FinalizeIntent.gitToken is the cross-provider carrier; K8sProvider prefers it over WARREN_GIT_TOKEN env. Any new credential-carrying field name must be added to SECRET_FIELDS in src/observability/log-redact.ts.

Bun's node:crypto createSign('RSA-SHA256') does NOT reject EC keys — it signs with the key's own algorithm silently (observed on Bun v1.2.23), unlike Node which throws. A test asserting a sign failure with an EC key therefore fails. Also: createPublicKey(publicKeyObject) throws ERR_CRYPTO_INVALID_KEY_OBJECT_TYPE under Bun.
resolution: Trigger the sign-failure path with a symmetric KeyObject (createSecretKey), which Bun does reject ('Invalid key object type secret, expected private'). Used in src/forge/github-app/installation-tokens.test.ts and jwt.test.ts.

name: k8s-app-mode-token-windows
description: K8s token windows under App mode (warren-c9ac): mint the clone credential at pod-spec time via K8sProviderDeps.mintGitCredential; gate the static env push-token fallback on forge credentialLifetime via allowStaticPushTokenFallback; pods re-mint salvage credentials over POST /runs/:id/git-credential rather than trusting the mounted Secret.

name: forge-credential-heartbeat
description: In-warren runtime health probes for forge credentials: force-mint pattern (bypass token cache — a cached hit proves nothing), surface via error-level structured log + MetricsRegistry counter (warren_forge_heartbeat_probe_total), boot from detector-wiring.ts alongside the watchdog, env knobs WARREN_FORGE_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_MS (30s floor clamp) / WARREN_FORGE_HEARTBEAT_DISABLED. Boot wiring goes in extracted modules because src/server/main/index.ts sits at exactly 500/500 check:size lines — trim comments to make room, never raise the budget.

A warren run that dies mid-work loses everything uncommitted: warren's salvage path produced no rescue ref and no bundle despite reap recording noChanges:false, and the branch it pushed was byte-identical to origin/main (branchPushed:true, commitsAhead:0). Observed on run_y3196c50a5qb — 29 minutes and $4.03 discarded. Trigger was openrouter credit exhaustion arriving mid-run as an empty completion (all-zero usage, content:[]), which the immediately-following re-dispatch confirmed with an explicit 402 naming openrouter_credits. Credit exhaustion is a foreseeable operating condition, not a freak fault.
resolution: Filed as warren-985e (P1). Interim mitigation: dogfood dispatch prompts now instruct agents to commit incrementally per unit of work rather than once at the end, so a mid-run fault costs one unit instead of the session. That depends on agent compliance and is not a fix. A pre-dispatch balance probe would have failed the run in 0s for $0 instead of 29min for $4.03.

description: A wrong doc citation propagates by imitation across independent agent runs. Comments citing 'forge-contract.md §4.2' (a section that does not exist — the doc has §4 and §4.1) were fixed in three files by one run, then independently RE-INTRODUCED in four reap-pipeline files by another run in the same session, then copied a third time. Each agent read a neighbouring comment and matched its spelling. Compounding hazard: k8s-migration.md §4.2 DOES exist, so a blanket search-replace across src/ would break correct references in src/runtime/k8s/.
resolution: Filed as warren-09dd (P3). Preferred fix is to ADD a §4.2 to forge-contract.md documenting mintGitCredentialSecret and its call-site contract — the section is arguably missing anyway (§4 states the decision, §4.1 covers long runs, nothing documents the helper every call site uses), and adding it resolves every existing pointer at once.

name: narrow-the-tracker-before-dispatch
description: When dispatching a warren run against a seeds issue whose body is a bare plan backref, the issue body is NOT a usable spec — the agent has nothing to build against and will guess. Fix it in the tracker BEFORE dispatching (sd update --description) rather than only in the prompt, so the run's own 'sd show <id>' reads the same scope the prompt states. Applied to warren-f8df this session: its body was a bare backref, so the narrowed scope plus pointers to forge-contract.md §4/§5/§7 were written into the issue first, then dispatched. The run landed all four deliverables in one clean pass with zero shepherding.

A plan's own acceptance criterion can become a trap once earlier phases land. pl-d1c9 criterion 4 said to delete 'AutoOpenPrConfig.token/.gitToken AND the by-value githubToken fields'. Phase 3 then made those githubToken PARAMETERS the intended per-spawn minted-credential delivery channel (src/forge/credentials.ts:5-13 — handlers mint via mintGitCredentialSecret and pass only the minted secret down the existing token/githubToken params). Following the criterion literally in the phase-5 deletion pass would have torn out the campaign's own mechanism.
resolution: The audit caught it pre-dispatch and the warren-5497 prompt carried an explicit correction: scope the deletion to CONFIG OBJECTS THAT HOLD a token, never to function parameters that CARRY a minted one, and stop if you find yourself removing a param mintGitCredentialSecret feeds. PR #844 landed correctly — it kept the params and only rewrote their doc comments. Lesson: re-verify late-phase acceptance criteria against the code the earlier phases actually shipped, not against the plan as written.

description: The merge-seeds-jsonl driver (landed in warren-9c90 to replace merge=union corruption) declares a merge unresolvable when two sides differ ONLY in a row's updatedAt timestamp. PR #842 conflicted against main over exactly two such rows (warren-3fe7.updatedAt, warren-5497.updatedAt) with no semantic disagreement — no status difference, no blockedBy difference. Because closing any plan child rewrites updatedAt across every sibling row, two concurrent warren runs reliably produce a hard conflict where none exists. Cost a dispatched repair run to clear.
resolution: Filed as warren-5f0d (P2). Fix is to treat updatedAt (and any pure-timestamp field) as auto-resolvable by max() in the driver's per-field resolution, reserving 'unresolvable' for fields where the sides genuinely disagree about content. The driver already does the hard parts correctly — it intersects blockedBy and takes closed where either side closed.

content: Flow endpoints in acceptance scenario 39: probe at the correct status, keep the leak scan, never silently skip. Use FLOW_ROUTE_EXPECTED_STATUS in scripts/acceptance/scenarios/39-public-exposure.ts. If a route must be exempted instead, the entry carries a comment naming the tracker id and stating why.

title: K8s Secret fallback under App mode routes through the authenticated callback
rationale: finalize-entrypoint.ts runs INSIDE the run pod and cannot hold an App private key, so it must ask the control plane rather than read a mounted Secret. The rejected alternative was a documented PAT-only degradation, which the design doc had allowed as an escape hatch (pl-d1c9 risk 6) but which would leave acceptance criterion 7 (a >1hr K8s run finalizes without a 401) permanently unmet under App mode. Routing through the callback also reuses a channel K8sProvider already owns, so it adds no new trust boundary.

description: GitHub's App-manifest flow rejects a 'state' key inside the manifest JSON ('"state" is not a permitted key') — the schema is closed. The CSRF nonce must ride the form's action URL as ?state=..., which GitHub echoes back on the callback redirect. The warren-bc4c spike note that 'state round-trips' held only for the query-param form; the mocked tests pinned the wrong shape and the bug surfaced on the first real registration attempt (2026-08-13).
resolution: Dropped state from GitHubAppManifest, moved it to the create URL as a query parameter, and pinned the corrected shape in tests (commit 0deb9511).

description: GitHub refuses ANY GitHub-App-token push that creates or updates a file under .github/workflows/ unless the App holds the workflows:write repository permission — the entire push is remote-rejected, not just the workflow file, so both the branch push and the rescue push die and the run ends finalize_failed with only a salvage bundle. A classic PAT's workflow scope covers this silently in PAT mode, so the gap only surfaces after switching WARREN_FORGE=app. First hit: run_qfc0xxgytf1p (warren-b34b) on dogfood day one, 2026-08-13.
resolution: Manifest now requests workflows:write (commit 6b0e6d08) so new registrations are born with it. Pre-existing Apps need the permission added in App settings AND the installation's approval of the permission request.

content: GitHub App-manifest schema: setup_url IS a documented manifest key (verified against live docs; GitHub appends ?installation_id=<id>&setup_action=install). state is NOT permitted inside the manifest. New server-rendered pages under /github-app/* must stay anonymous-policy, CSP default-src 'none', no inline script, and be enumerated in the SPECTATOR_ROUTES test in src/server/handlers/index.test.ts. registration.ts sits exactly at the 500-line check:size budget.

description: External contributor PR #982 (PARS-Agent tooling) mangled every two-byte UTF-8 § in touched files into a single 0x10 control byte — renders as a deletion in diffs and silently breaks grep '§12.5'. When a contributor diff seems to strip unicode punctuation, hexdump the line before assuming an intentional edit. Also: forks with maintainerCanModify=false plus strict up-to-date branch protection make the PR unmergeable in place.
resolution: Restored all 11 § via perl s/\x10/\xc2\xa7/g; landed the fork PR via a second branch (#989) carrying the contributor's commits plus review fixes, then pushed a tree-identical 'git merge -s ours <pr-head>' to main so #982 flipped to Merged with authorship intact.

title: Forges stay in-core; no remote-forge bridge (2026-08-20)
rationale: The forge market is 3-4 near-identical APIs (GitLab, Forgejo/Gitea, maybe Bitbucket) versus the long tail of trackers, so in-core registry arms cost less than a second wire protocol plus conformance suite. Credential minting (forge-contract.md §4) is the forge's load-bearing job and should not gain a process hop. The contract already has room for a second arm and scenario 40 proves the domain is forge-neutral.

name: hot-forge-activation
description: Hot-activation of a boot-resolved seam: wrap the boot instance in a delegating proxy (HotForge in src/forge/hot-forge.ts) and thread the proxy everywhere, then swap the delegate on activation — avoids touching every consumer closure; heartbeat wiring unwraps via .current (warren-b504)
